title: New Research Confirms Risks of Drinking Very Hot Beverages
subtitle: Large-scale study suggests cooling down your tea or coffee could help protect your health

summary.en: A major new study has found that drinking tea and coffee at very high temperatures may triple the risk of a specific type of throat cancer. Researchers analyzed the habits of nearly one million people in the UK over 14 years. The findings show that the temperature of a drink is a key factor in long-term health. Experts suggest that waiting for drinks to cool down can significantly reduce these risks. This research supports earlier global findings regarding the dangers of consuming very hot liquids.
summary.zh: 一項新的大型研究發現，飲用極高溫的茶與咖啡可能會使罹患特定類型喉癌的風險增加三倍。研究人員分析了英國近一百萬人在十四年間的習慣。研究結果顯示，飲品溫度是影響長期健康的關鍵因素。專家建議，等待飲品冷卻可以顯著降低這些風險。這項研究支持了先前關於攝取極熱液體具有危險性的全球性發現。

paragraphs.en: Following our recent reports on the potential health risks of hot beverages, new data has provided a clearer picture of how our daily habits affect our long-term health. A massive study, published recently in the International Journal of Cancer, has confirmed that drinking tea and coffee at very high temperatures can triple the risk of developing a specific type of throat cancer. This research, led by Dr. Keren Papier at the University of Oxford, is the largest of its kind, tracking the habits and health of almost 980,000 people in the UK over a period of 14 years.
paragraphs.zh: 繼我們近期報導關於熱飲潛在的健康風險後，新的數據讓我們更清楚地了解日常習慣如何影響長期健康。一份近期發表於《國際癌症期刊》（International Journal of Cancer）的大型研究證實，飲用極高溫的茶與咖啡，可能會使罹患特定類型喉癌的風險增加三倍。這項研究由牛津大學（University of Oxford）的凱倫·帕皮爾（Keren Papier）博士領導，是同類研究中規模最大的一項，追蹤了英國近九十八萬人在十四年間的習慣與健康狀況。

paragraphs.en: The study focuses on oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), a form of cancer that affects the foodpipe. According to The Guardian Health, the findings show a clear link between the temperature of drinks and the risk of this disease. While the study did not find that hot drinks increase the risk of all types of throat cancer, the connection to SCC is significant. Researchers noted that the risk increases not only with the temperature of the drink but also with how often a person consumes them. Specifically, people who drank six or more hot drinks every day faced a 71% higher risk of this cancer compared to those who drank fewer.
paragraphs.zh: 該研究聚焦於食道鱗狀細胞癌（SCC），這是一種影響食道的癌症。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，研究結果顯示飲品溫度與此疾病風險之間存在明確關聯。雖然研究並未發現熱飲會增加所有類型喉癌的風險，但與食道鱗狀細胞癌的關聯性相當顯著。研究人員指出，風險不僅隨飲品溫度升高而增加，也與飲用頻率有關。具體而言，每天飲用六杯或更多熱飲的人，與飲用較少的人相比，罹患此類癌症的風險高出百分之七十一。

paragraphs.en: This new information builds upon previous concerns raised by the World Health Organization. In 2016, the International Agency for Research on Cancer identified hot drinks as a probable cause of cancer. The current theory is that very hot liquids cause physical damage to the cells that line the foodpipe. Over time, this repeated heat damage may lead to the development of cancer. These latest findings from the UK mirror similar trends previously observed in studies across Asia, Africa, South America, and the Middle East, where drinking very hot tea or herbal drinks like mate has long been a subject of health concern.
paragraphs.zh: 這項新資訊建立在世界衛生組織（World Health Organization）先前提出的疑慮之上。二零一六年，國際癌症研究機構（International Agency for Research on Cancer）將熱飲列為可能的致癌物。目前的理論認為，極高溫的液體會對食道內壁細胞造成物理性損傷。長久下來，這種反覆的熱損傷可能導致癌症發生。這項來自英國的最新發現，與先前在亞洲、非洲、南美洲及中東地區的研究趨勢相呼應，在這些地區，飲用極熱的茶或如瑪黛茶（mate）等草本飲品，長期以來一直是健康關注的議題。

paragraphs.en: One of the most important aspects of this study is that it relies on how people describe their own drinking habits. Participants were asked to categorize their preferred drink temperature as “very hot,” “hot,” or “warm.” The researchers found that even without measuring the exact temperature of every cup, the trend was clear: those who preferred “very hot” drinks were at a much higher risk. The study team suggests that this is a preventable health issue. They estimate that one in seven cases of this specific cancer in the UK could be avoided if people simply chose to drink their tea or coffee at a “hot” or “warm” temperature instead of “very hot.”
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究最重要的面向之一，在於它依賴受試者對自身飲用習慣的描述。參與者被要求將偏好的飲品溫度歸類為「極熱」、「熱」或「溫」。研究人員發現，即便沒有測量每一杯飲品的確切溫度，趨勢依然明確：偏好「極熱」飲品的人風險高出許多。研究團隊認為這是一個可預防的健康問題。他們估計，如果人們選擇將茶或咖啡的溫度控制在「熱」或「溫」而非「極熱」，英國七分之一的此類癌症病例是可以避免的。

paragraphs.en: It is important to note that while this study highlights the risks of heat, other factors like smoking and alcohol consumption remain major causes of throat cancer. However, the researchers believe that health authorities can use these new findings to encourage simple, effective lifestyle changes. By waiting just a few minutes for a drink to cool down, individuals can significantly lower their risk without giving up their favorite beverages entirely. The study suggests that the goal should be to consume drinks at a temperature well below the “very hot” category.
paragraphs.zh: 值得注意的是，儘管這項研究強調了高溫的風險，但吸菸與飲酒等其他因素仍是喉癌的主要成因。然而，研究人員相信衛生主管機關可以利用這些新發現，鼓勵民眾進行簡單且有效的日常生活調整。只要多花幾分鐘等待飲品冷卻，個人就能在不完全放棄喜愛飲品的情況下，顯著降低風險。研究建議，目標應是將飲用溫度控制在「極熱」等級以下。

paragraphs.en: As we continue to look at how daily habits influence our health, this study serves as a helpful reminder that small changes can have a big impact. While the findings are specific to a Western European population, the consistency with global data suggests that the advice to let drinks cool down is universal. Moving forward, health experts hope that public awareness will lead to a decrease in the number of people diagnosed with this form of cancer. For now, the best advice remains simple: enjoy your tea or coffee, but give it a little time to reach a safer, more comfortable temperature before you take that first sip.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著我們持續探討日常習慣如何影響健康，這項研究提醒我們，微小的改變也能產生巨大的影響。雖然研究結果針對的是西歐族群，但與全球數據的一致性顯示，讓飲品冷卻後再飲用的建議具有普世價值。展望未來，健康專家希望大眾意識的提升能減少此類癌症的確診人數。目前最好的建議依然簡單：享受你的茶或咖啡，但在喝下第一口之前，給它一點時間降至更安全、更舒適的溫度。

keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（鏡子），這裡作動詞用。文中：These latest findings from the UK mirror similar trends previously observed in studies across Asia, Africa, South America, and the Middle East, where drinking very hot tea or herbal drinks like mate has long been a subject of health concern.
由動詞與副詞組成，意思與單字原意不同。文中：By waiting just a few minutes for a drink to cool down, individuals can significantly lower their risk without giving up their favorite beverages entirely.

quiz.question: According to the study, what specific condition must be met for a person to face a 71% higher risk of oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma?

options.A: Drinking tea or coffee at a 'very hot' temperature exclusively.
options.B: Consuming six or more hot drinks on a daily basis.
options.C: Having a history of both smoking and frequent hot drink consumption.
options.D: Drinking hot beverages for more than 14 years.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，研究指出每天飲用六杯或更多熱飲的人，罹患此類癌症的風險比飲用較少的人高出 71%。選項 A 雖然提到了「非常熱」的溫度與風險有關，但 71% 的數據是針對「飲用頻率」而非單純溫度。選項 C 雖提到抽菸是其他風險因素，但文章並未將其與 71% 的數據連結。選項 D 的 14 年是研究的追蹤期間，而非導致風險增加的條件。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the methodology of the study regarding temperature measurements?

options.A: The researchers used high-precision thermometers to ensure accuracy.
options.B: The study's findings are potentially unreliable because they lack objective temperature data.
options.C: Subjective perceptions of temperature were sufficient to identify a clear health trend.
options.D: Participants were trained to measure their drinks to ensure consistent data collection.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，研究依賴參與者對飲品溫度的自我描述（「非常熱」、「熱」、「溫」）。儘管缺乏精確的溫度計數據，研究人員仍發現了明確的風險趨勢，這暗示了主觀感受已足夠反映出健康風險的關聯性。選項 A 與 D 與文中「without measuring the exact temperature」的敘述矛盾。選項 B 雖然提到缺乏客觀數據，但文章並未指出這導致研究結果不可靠，反而強調了趨勢的明確性。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, the word 'mirror' is used to describe the relationship between the UK study and previous global studies. What does 'mirror' mean in this context?

options.A: To reflect or correspond to similar patterns.
options.B: To copy something exactly without any changes.
options.C: To reverse the findings of previous research.
options.D: To look at oneself in a reflective surface.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，mirror 的意思是「反映」或「與...相似」，指英國的研究結果與亞洲、非洲等地先前的研究發現呈現一致的趨勢。選項 B 錯誤，因為研究只是結果相似，並非完全複製過程。選項 C 錯誤，因為 mirror 在此處表示一致性而非對立。選項 D 是該詞的字面意思，在此處並不適用，因為這不是在描述照鏡子。

quiz.question: Which statement best summarizes the main message of the article?

options.A: People should stop drinking tea and coffee entirely to avoid throat cancer.
options.B: The risk of throat cancer is primarily caused by the chemical composition of tea and coffee.
options.C: New research suggests that the temperature of hot beverages is a major, yet preventable, health risk.
options.D: The study proves that smoking and alcohol are less dangerous than drinking hot tea.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章的核心主旨是透過最新的大規模研究，指出飲用「非常熱」的飲料與食道癌風險增加有關，並強調這是一個可以透過簡單改變（如等待飲料冷卻）來預防的健康問題。選項 A 與文中建議「不必完全放棄喜愛的飲料」相違背。選項 B 錯誤，因為文章歸因於熱度造成的物理損傷，而非成分。選項 D 錯誤，文章僅提到抽菸與酒精仍是主要原因，並未比較誰更危險。
